sub_site: cerebrospinal fluid (multiple sclerosis and other neurological conditions)

evidence.quote: We conducted a metagenomic survey in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from 28 MS patients and 15 patients suffering other type of neurological conditions
For construction of metagenomics libraries, the Nextera XT (Illumina) technology was used
Demultiplexed reads were aligned against a customized database using the ultrafast metagenomic classification package Kraken
Thirty-four out of 43 samples contained <1% bacterial reads, which we regard as cross- or environmental contamination

notes: No negative controls; authors treat samples with <1% bacterial reads as contamination and suspect rack-neighbour cross-contamination from sample 3C. P. acnes flagged as known library contaminant; Alteromonas mediterranea also 'most ubiquitous' (likely background, not explicitly called contaminant). Ralstonia only as spurious adapter-like hits of viral reads (not recorded). Full per-sample taxa in Supplementary Table 1 (not converted). Conclusion: CSF generally free of microbial DNA, with two bacteria-rich exceptions.
